workingTitle: Two faint galaxies light up beside a nearly pristine reservoir of cosmic gas
freshness: MNRAS-accepted open-access paper posted to arXiv on October 26, 2026; selected within the preferred 15-day window.
coreFacts: Keck/KCWI detected two high-confidence Lyman-alpha emitting galaxies in the wider environment of a damped Lyman-alpha absorber at redshift 3.078.
The neutral-hydrogen cloud has measured oxygen abundance [O/H] = -3.08 +/- 0.05 and an iron abundance upper limit [Fe/H] < -3.66 at 2 sigma, placing it among the most metal-poor DLAs known.
The galaxies lie 66 and 137 physical kiloparsecs in projection from the quasar sightline and were detected with signal-to-noise ratios per spatial pixel of 6 and 5.
Their Lyman-alpha luminosities are (3.8 +/- 0.6) x 10^41 and (3.2 +/- 0.8) x 10^41 erg/s, implying star-formation-rate lower limits of 0.34 and 0.29 solar masses per year.
The faint, narrow, unresolved sources may be metal-poor galaxies, but their metallicities have not been measured directly and their physical connection to the absorber remains uncertain.
caveats: The galaxies are detected near the absorber in projection and redshift, but the data do not prove that either is the absorber's host or that all three occupy one structure.
The field does not contain a statistically significant excess of Lyman-alpha emitters compared with adjacent redshift intervals.
Low metallicity in the two galaxies is inferred from several indirect properties; rest-frame optical spectroscopy is needed to measure it.
The paper is accepted by MNRAS and publicly available as an author preprint, but its journal version was not yet the accessible source used in this run.
sourceStatus: Full open-access MNRAS-accepted paper read; measurements and limitations verified against the primary source.
